sections.value:
**Performance: block** at `37056e3e0776866578461068ad0d623d6749a6be`.

Full PR-owned review against `c3895da518aad2047749b87dc9c6663592e357e2`. The checks share the existing 60-second watchdog timer, but the new read-saving size cache can hide the context changes the feature is meant to report. CI is green; it does not cover that cache invalidation case.

## P153-F001: cached idle sizes do not follow new context reports

`pa_presence.rs:792-803` refreshes a seat only when currently working, seen working in the previous round, or absent from the size map. Initial unknown/failed reads still insert a map entry (`806-827`); that entry is then treated as cached even with no known size.

`/v1/activity` updates a separate `ReportedContext` map (`http/fyi.rs:249-255`). Neither that update nor a new idle activity event invalidates the watchdog's size cache. A concrete missed crossing is:

1. One round caches an idle Copilot seat as unknown or below 600k.
2. The seat takes a turn entirely between two 60-second rounds. Its activity posts publish working then idle, with a new context report above 600k.
3. The next round sees idle again, `was_working` is false, and the cache entry exists. It never asks the updated status overlay, so no large-seat FYI is produced.

The same stale-cache condition can miss rearming after a short turn/compaction. The current large-seat test explicitly keeps an idle seat's old large claim after the underlying size changes (`pa_watchdog_tests.rs:2656-2684`); the context-overlay test checks the source directly, not this composed cache.

Invalidate cached sizes using report/activity/session generation, including a new report arriving after an initially unknown read. Do not fix this by rereading every idle transcript every minute. Add a focused composed test: cache unknown/below threshold, publish a new idle report after working/idle transitions between rounds, and verify the crossing; also cover rearm. This is a source-level finding, not a local reproduction. Bobcat has the pointer.

## Per-round cost

N = seats in the round snapshot, S = presence scopes, P = PAs needing a turn read, C = retained claims, B = due size reads.

| Check/surface | Rate, scaling and limits |
|---|---|
| Common scope/claim work | Once per existing 60-second round: one full `presence_claims` read plus schema check. Designated-prime lookup now also happens with no PA. Scope construction uses cached repository keys and cloned seat descriptors. Claim pruning uses repeated seat searches, O(CN); fleet descendant placement scans candidates per scope and walks at most 16 ancestors with linear seat lookups, potentially O(SN²) at that fixed depth. These are not constant per-scope comparisons. |
| Missing PA, ac-0002 | Pure scope comparisons each round; no message until the 20-minute active/missing threshold. A send takes one INSERT claim and one settlement UPDATE/DELETE, plus existing delivery/audit work. Positive rearm evidence removes an existing claim; it does not delete a nonexistent claim every quiet round. |
| Dormant/unresponsive, ac-0003/4 | P indexed `LIMIT 1` activity queries per round (plus schema/read-transaction work), using the existing `spine_by_seat_kind` index. Dormant wake at 30 minutes builds the ordinary digest, adding its existing status/card/queued-request reads. Unresponsive alert follows ten minutes later. Claims cap a queued/held/successful stretch; refused/failed delivery releases its claim and can retry on subsequent rounds. No independent retry timer. |
| Large seats, ac-0005 | B status tasks per round for currently working, previously working or uncached seats; an idle cached entry is skipped, causing F001. Reads share the existing three-second batch deadline and at most one outstanding read per seat. Underlying transcript status still runs before the reported-context overlay. A completed read can be repeated by a digest and this refresh in the same round; the outstanding-read guard is not a once-per-round cache. Crossings take one claim/settlement per seat and one combined held FYI per scope. |
| Context activity, ac-0006 | The usage-info callback updates two cached scalars and does not post by itself. The next existing activity-state post carries them: no new timer, RPC to collect usage, or ordinary additional post. A 400/422 compatibility refusal can add one state-only retry, then permanently suppresses context fields for that bridge. The daemon adds an in-memory mutex/map update per accepted report; the overlay locks/clones one report after the existing transcript read. |
| Memory/audit | Fleet vectors and size snapshots clone descriptors/model strings. Size/PA/scope state is pruned, but reported-context and changed-verdict bookkeeping retain entries for encountered identities; missing-scope claims persist until positive rearm evidence. No hard cardinality cap is introduced. Audits are on verdict changes, not one event per unchanged check per round. |
| **Launch qualification** | No new executable launch site or timer. Repository placement still launches the existing resolved Git helper on a new folder. Failed placement is negatively cached for 600 seconds, then retried: an existing unplaced directory can cost about one Git launch per ten minutes, not one per daemon lifetime. Real notification delivery may use existing transport launches; the data checks' no-launch property is not a universal no-child guarantee. |

Known Copilot context now participates in the existing >400k/idle-over-one-hour cold-wake guard; unknown size remains non-refusing. That intentional eligibility change reuses the existing admission/status path. F84's price/billing issue is outside this review.

The shared status deadline bounds caller waiting for one batch, not background-reader lifetime or the whole round. Sequential PA queries, cold repository placement and notification/digest work can extend a round; no new overall wall-time cap is introduced.

## Zero-launch and CI proof

The isolated `presence_launches` binary has one test, so its process-global counter is not contaminated by another test in that binary. After placing existing Git folders, 45 simulated rounds generate each of the four notification kinds once without increasing the recorded daemon launch counter. A fresh Git folder increases the placement counter by exactly one: a real positive control.

Its store/registry/queue are real, but liveness/transport/session-status use test adapters, and recipients have no bound processes. Thus this proves cached-repository check/notification admission work is launch-free in that fixture, not actual Claude socket delivery, wall-clock negative-cache expiry, or whole-machine launch cost. Simulated minutes do not advance the real `Instant`-based negative-cache TTL.

[CI 42365178455](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42365178455) attempts **1 and 2** both succeed at this exact head. Latest JUnit records **2,076 executed cases, zero failures/errors**; five Rust tests were skipped separately. Presence clocks/restart claims, dormant and large-seat behavior, reported-context overlay, Copilot cold-guard parity, the isolated launch test and all six spawn guards ran successfully. Node 22's native gate passed **325/325**, including usage-info piggyback/fallback. Latest delivers **42365832559** succeeded; an earlier superseded delivers run was cancelled, not failed. GitHub is CLEAN.

## Migration 0039 before 0038

**Confirmed from source**, provided the later build keeps `SCHEMA_VERSION >= 39` and includes the unchanged applied 0039 migration. `store/src/migrate.rs:154-202` always calls `MIGRATIONS.run`, even when the pragma is already current, then restores the pragma to the compiled schema version. SQLx **0.8.6**, pinned in Cargo.lock, [checks applied versions individually and applies each absent version](https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/blob/v0.8.6/sqlx-core/src/migrate/migrator.rs); it does not skip all versions below the highest applied number. A later pending 0038 therefore runs even with 0039 in the ledger. A build accidentally lowering the compiled version to 38 would refuse before migrating. No future-0038 runtime exercise was performed.

No local builds, tests, probes, injected fleet traffic or review-tree edits. After F001 is repaired and deployment authorized, the matched live reading remains owed: counter sites, whole-machine rate, daemon CPU/RSS, scope/seat/read cardinalities and actual elapsed time. The current zero-launch fixture is not that deployment proof.
